text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The decision by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to halt a key aid package to Kenya because of corruption sends shock waves through the foreign exchange and stock markets and will force the government to tighten its belt.
- John Koech, minister of state in the office of the president, announces his resignation from the cabinet citing frustration.
- Attorney-General Amos Wako publishes a bill to amend or repeal repressive laws.
- The IMF stops a crucial three-year programme to Kenya.
- Parliamentary opposition leader Michael Wamalwa says the IMF decision to withold aid was inevitable.
- President Daniel arap Moi said the government will not succumb to ultimatums, intimidation and threats.
- Kenyans must brace for tough economic times ahead of an IMF decision to suspend aid.
- Police Commissioner Duncan Wachira appoints deputy director of Criminal Investigation Peter Mbuvi to lead a team to probe the death of former police commissioner Peter Kilonzo.
